_schema: sdlc-kit/sdlc.config.schema.json — the kit lives outside this repo (see .gitignore)

gates.title: Rule 1 — core never imports a domain
gates.fix: The fix is a registration or a callback on the core side, never an import. If the gate is being worked around, that is the bug.

gates.title: Every publishable package is importable by an adopter
gates.fix: An entry point in main/types/exports either does not exist, is not covered by `files`, or is TypeScript source. Run `pnpm build` first — the gate reads built output. A .ts entry point cannot work at all: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING), which is what made every package in this repo uninstallable until 2026-09-11. If a package is not meant to be installed, mark it private.

gates.title: Releasable — one version, a CHANGELOG section and the LICENSE in every package
gates.fix: Every publishable package must carry the same version, the root package.json's license and a byte-identical copy of the root LICENSE, and CHANGELOG.md must have a non-empty section for that version. After editing LICENSE, copy it into each publishable package. The release workflow also runs this with --tag, which requires the tag to be v<version> and the section to carry a date instead of 'unreleased'.

gates.title: The packed tarballs install into a project outside this repository and run on Node 20
gates.fix: Read which step failed and on which Node. A dependency that only resolves inside the workspace, a file reached by a checkout-only path, a Node API newer than 20, or a bin that is TypeScript source all install cleanly and fail on the adopter's first command. The scratch project is kept for inspection.

gates.title: adapter/ matches what packages/ builds
gates.fix: adapter/ is committed build output — an adopter copies it as it sits and cannot regenerate it on their machine. Rebuild and commit it with the change that caused it: pnpm adapter:build. Committed build output with no staleness gate is a failure mode this repository has hit three times; see critical-infrastructure.md.

gates.title: A copy of adapter/ runs with nothing installed, and writes nothing into the app
gates.fix: The premise of ADR-018 is "copy the folder and run it". This copies adapter/ and a fixture application into a scratch directory OUTSIDE the repository — no node_modules anywhere above it — and runs init, build and doctor for real, then fingerprints the application to prove Rule 16. Run it with --keep to inspect the scratch project. Every failure found while building the adapter was a failure of the BUNDLE in a bare directory rather than of the source, which is why no unit test replaces this.

gates.title: Rule 15 — a prompt never interpolates unfenced input
gates.fix: Wrap the value: fence('what this is', value), or redactTag('tagname', value) if the prompt already delimits with tags. If the prompt genuinely needs no fence, say why in the source with a `// rule15-ok: <reason>` comment next to the call. Note what this gate can and cannot see: it proves a fence was applied near a prompt, not that it covered the right value — fencing legitimately happens upstream. Reading for that is the boundary-auditor agent's job.

gates.title: Adversarial bucket against a real model (local only)
gates.fix: A NEW entry made the router select a forbidden capability. Establish which layer moved before recording it: did the fence stop applying (check-prompt-fencing.mjs), or did the model disregard an intact fence (Finding 14's case — print the prompt and count the delimiters before assuming a bypass)? This gate is deliberately absent from CI: GitHub Actions has no model server, which is exactly why the adversarial bucket passed trivially there for so long and why three of Finding 14's four violations had never been seen. It skips cleanly with a loud message when Ollama is unreachable.

gates.title: Rule 8 — the device is the source of truth
gates.fix: A remote host in a runtime string literal falsifies the local-inference claim for every adopter. Loopback is fine. Nothing downloads assets any more (ADR-018), so there is no longer an exception for a pinned manifest — widening this gate to clear a failure is the wrong fix. Two things it cannot see: OLLAMA_HOST can be pointed anywhere by the environment, and a host assembled at run time from parts.

gates.title: Rule 2 — the model never returns a number
gates.fix: A number the model returns is a number the model computed. Have code compute it — the query engine sums, code does the arithmetic — and let the model choose the capability and read values out of the utterance. If the number is genuinely never shown to a user, say why in the source with `// rule2-ok: <reason>`. This guards the model's output schema, not arithmetic our own code does on it: no user-visible number is rendered anywhere yet, so the render-path test the register used to propose would assert over an empty set.

gates.title: Every relative documentation link resolves
gates.fix: The named target does not exist. Either the file moved (update the link) or the link was always wrong. Note this gate only sees markdown links — a path in a JSON string or a code comment is not checked.

gates.title: WP-46 — shipped indexes, thresholds and browser decisions follow their inputs
gates.fix: Something upstream of eval/frameworks/family/generated changed: normalize(), the encoder, capabilityDocument(), or a registry. Regenerate with rebuild-indexes.mjs, then calibrate-registries.mjs --embedder hashing, and commit the result with the change that caused it. Never hand-edit these files: they are measurements.

gates.title: The committed scorecard still describes what the fixture apps decide
gates.fix: Something changed what the router decides on the generated registries — a description, a trigger, normalize(), or a threshold. If it was intended, regenerate with `node --experimental-strip-types eval/frameworks/evaluate-golden.mjs --embedder hashing` and commit the scorecard in the same commit as the cause. Timing is excluded from the comparison, so this is never a slow-machine failure.

gates.title: WP-45 — the shipped widget has no serious or critical a11y violations
gates.fix: Run node tooling/scripts/check-accessibility.mjs and read eval/a11y/axe.json. This is the automated half only: colour contrast, announcement order and anything as-rendered are eval/a11y/NVDA-CHECKLIST.md, which a person runs.

gates.title: The documented one-line script tag starts, styles and routes under a strict Content-Security-Policy, in a real browser
gates.fix: Read which check failed. A policy violation names the directive: no inline <style> or <script>, no style="" attribute (set styles through the CSSOM, as widget.ts and start() do). "Unstyled" means the constructed stylesheet did not apply. Skips on a machine with no Chrome, Chromium or Edge; set NEXTGEN_BROWSER. Fails under CI instead of skipping.

gates.title: Hooks identical in .claude/ and sdlc-kit/runtime/
gates.fix: Hooks are config-driven and must be byte-identical in both places. Copy the correct version over the other. Skills and agents are exempt — those are generated per repo and are SUPPOSED to differ. Skips cleanly when sdlc-kit/ is absent, since the kit is gitignored and not present in a fresh clone.

gates.title: Rule 14 — shipped thresholds are the calibrated ones
gates.fix: config.ts no longer matches the calibration output. Re-run `pnpm router:calibrate` if the corpus changed; otherwise someone hand-edited a threshold, which is exactly what Rule 14 exists to prevent. Hand-tuning has cost accuracy three times here.

gates.title: Strict TypeScript across the workspace
gates.fix: Read the file:line and the error. Do not widen a type to silence it.

gates.title: Unit tests, every package
gates.fix: Name the failing test and its first assertion before changing anything.

gates.title: Rule 10 — >=3 examples per capability, across every registry in the tree
gates.fix: Usually a capability with fewer than three examples. Add real paraphrases, not variations of one sentence. Since ADR-018 this validates every registry found by glob rather than one domain's, so a failure names the file: fix that registry, or the generator that emitted it.

gates.title: Deterministic router floor (stages 1+2, hashing encoder)
gates.fix: Exits non-zero BY DESIGN — with stage 3 disabled it cannot meet absolute accuracy targets and is not meant to. What gates is the scorecard comparison below.

gates.title: Golden-set regression against the scorecard committed at HEAD
gates.fix: Identify which bucket dropped. The usual culprit is a new capability whose description overlaps an existing one. Fix at the declaration — NEVER by raising a threshold. This compares your working tree against the scorecard committed at HEAD, so it only has something to say after `pnpm router:floor` has re-run; CI does the same with a baseline copied aside before the run.

gates.title: Dependency CVE scan
gates.fix: Upgrade, or record an accepted risk in .claude/docs/security.md with an owner and a date.

postEdit.remind: A registry changed. Rule 10 needs >=3 examples — run `pnpm registry:check`. If this was the router's frozen fixture, the committed scorecards were produced from it and `check-scorecard.mjs` compares against them: see packages/core-intent/eval/README.md before changing it at all. Then `pnpm router:floor` to check nothing crowded its neighbours.

Eval asset changed. Thresholds come from `pnpm router:calibrate`, never from hand-tuning — a hand-tuned threshold encodes the last utterance you happened to try. If a bucket regressed, fix the capability description, not the threshold.
